extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for filing a reply brief to an examiner's answer in a patent appeal and for paying the fee to forward an appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, including timing, content, format, extensions, and consequences of non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for petition to Director under §1.181
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of the primary examiner’s failure to designate a rejection as a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer must be by way of a petition to the Director under §1.181 filed within two months from the entry of the examiner’s answer and before the filing of any reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure of appellant to timely file such a petition will constitute a waiver of any arguments that a rejection must be designated as a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect if petition granted to designate new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision granting a petition under §1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer will provide a two-month time period in which appellant must file a reply under §1.111 to reopen prosecution before the primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On failure to timely file a reply under §1.111, the appeal will stand dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect if petition denied
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision refusing to grant a petition under §1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer will provide a two-month time period in which appellant may file only a single reply brief under §41.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This one reply brief is the exclusive reply available in that situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief treated as withdrawal of petition if filed before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply brief under §41.41 is filed within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer and on or after the filing of a petition under §1.181, but before a decision on the petition, the reply brief will be treated as a request to withdraw the petition and to maintain the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the reply in that window effectively abandons the petition and keeps the appeal alive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time not allowed under §1.136(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under §1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to the time periods set forth for filing reply briefs or related petitions/fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.136(b) for extensions of time to reply for patent applications and §1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single reply brief as a matter of right and its timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 41.41(a)(1), appellant may file a single reply brief as a matter of right within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner’s answer, or a decision refusing to grant a petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally appellant is not required to file a reply brief and if none is filed the application will be forwarded to the Board for decision on the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content prohibition: no new amendments or new evidence in reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.116 for amendments, affidavits or other evidence filed after final action but before or on the same date of filing an appeal and §41.33 for amendments, affidavits or other evidence filed after the date of filing the appeal. Any new amendment must be submitted in papers separate from the reply brief; a paper that contains an amendment is not a reply brief and will not be entered simply because it is characterized as a reply brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on arguments in reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Any argument raised in the reply brief which was not raised in the appeal brief, or is not responsive to an argument raised in the examiner's answer, including any designated new ground of rejection, will not be considered by the Board for purposes of the present appeal, unless good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply briefs must be confined to responding to matters already joined in the appeal and the examiner’s answer; new independent arguments are generally waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a reply brief is required to maintain the appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant is required to file either a reply brief to maintain the appeal or a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 to reopen prosecution when the examiner’s answer designates a new ground of rejection or a substitute examiner’s answer responds to a Board remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant requests that the appeal be maintained in response to a new ground of rejection, the appellant must file a reply brief to address each new ground of rejection set forth in the answer in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv) within two months from the mailing of the answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format/contents required in a reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The reply brief should include the following items, with each item starting on a separate page, to follow the other requirements of a brief as set forth in 37 CFR 41.37(c): (A) Identification page setting forth appellant’s name(s), application number, filing date, title of the invention, name of the examiner, art unit, and the title of the paper (i.e., Reply Brief); (B) Argument page(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §41.37(c) formatting requirements for briefs; each required item must start on a separate page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of reply brief filed in response to substitute examiner’s answer that contains amendment/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply brief is filed in response to a substitute examiner’s answer under 37 CFR 41.50(a) that was written in response to a remand by the Board, any reply brief accompanied by an amendment, affidavit or other evidence will be treated as a request that prosecution be reopened before the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a reply will not be treated solely as a reply brief and may change the procedural posture to reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to file required reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant fails to file a reply brief or a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 within two months from the mailing of the examiner’s answer that contains a new ground of rejection, or a substitute examiner’s answer under 37 CFR 41.50(a), the appeal may be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 1207.03 and 1207.05 for dismissal procedures and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s role after receipt of reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41, jurisdiction over the appeal passes to the Board; normally the examiner does not need to acknowledge the reply brief and will not have an opportunity for further argument prior to a decision by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the Board may remand the appeal to the examiner to furnish a substitute examiner’s answer responsive to the remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to pay appeal forwarding fee (§41.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must pay the fee set forth in §37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner's answer, or a decision refusing to grant a petition under §1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in an examiner's answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee is not paid within this period the appeal will stand dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay appeal forwarding fee results in dismissal
rubrics_metrics.description: On failure to pay the fee set forth in §37 CFR 41.20(b)(4) within the required period, the appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal is dismissed by rule; the examiner should proceed as indicated in MPEP §1215 regardless of whether a separate paper is mailed dismissing the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for paying appeal forwarding fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under §1.136(a) are not applicable to the time period for paying the appeal forwarding fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §1.136(b) for extensions of time to reply for patent applications and §1.550(c) for extensions for ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and recommended timing for paying appeal forwarding fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's answer should provide notice that the appeal forwarding fee must be paid within the requisite time period or the appeal will stand dismissed; it is preferable that appellants pay this fee at the same time any reply brief is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of form PTO/AIA/34 (Certification and Transmittal of Appeal Forwarding Fee) is suggested. An applicant who files a reply brief and authorizes the Office to charge any fees related to that submission will not have authorized the Office to charge the appeal forwarding fee unless clearly authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal forwarding fee waiver conditions (pre-March 19, 2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to pay the appeal forwarding fee is waived when the appeal brief fee was paid before March 19, 2013, so applicants who paid the appeal brief fee before that date will not be required to pay the appeal forwarding fee for the same appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This waiver only applied where the appeal brief and its corresponding appeal brief fee were filed before March 19, 2013 and where applicant seeks to reinstate an appeal in such application prior to the Board issuing a decision on the earlier appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal forwarding fee is premature before examiner’s answer
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal forwarding fee is premature if the fee is filed prior to the mailing of the examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office cannot accept a general authorization to pay the appeal forwarding fee because appeal fees are in 37 CFR 41.20 and not in 37 CFR 1.16 to 1.18. Applicant should be clear in an authorization that the fee is directed to payment of the appeal forwarding fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability: fee does not apply to inter partes reexamination appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: The appeal forwarding fee does not apply to inter partes reexamination appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only ex parte reexamination and patent application appeals are subject to the forwarding fee rules described in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical example of fee application after prior appeal and RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant filed an appeal brief and paid the appeal brief fee on March 18, 2013 and a final Board decision issued on March 16, 2015, then after filing an RCE and later filing a new notice of appeal and appeal brief, the applicant would be required to pay the appeal forwarding fee within the period specified in 37 CFR 41.45(a) to continue with the new appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This example illustrates that prior payment of an appeal brief fee before March 19, 2013 does not immunize later appeals filed after prosecution (e.g., following an RCE) from the forwarding fee unless the waiver conditions still apply.
